summary: createHeadlessProof gains readOnly (default false, so the pmdoc generators keep the server's document refusals). The SPA engine (markdown-engine.ts) passes readOnly: true, which installs remarkReadOnlyDirectives (new legion-owned file packages/proof-editor/src/read-only-directives.ts) in place of remarkTypedBlocks: paragraph-line directive refusals are not applied, and a container directive the block schema refuses (unknown name, undeclared attribute, refused value, or any directive with no schema) is replaced in place by a literal paragraph of its opening line, its children (label paragraph dropped, recursively processed, formatted), and a literal paragraph of its closing fence when the source closes it. block-schema.ts exports typedBlockRefusal(schema, node), the one rule visit and the read-only transform both use.
tasks: 1. packages/proof-editor/src/block-schema.ts: export typedBlockRefusal(schema, node): string | undefined returning the exact strings visit/directiveAttrs throw today; visit throws its result.

2. packages/proof-editor/src/read-only-directives.ts (new, legion-owned, biome-checked): remarkReadOnlyDirectives(schema?: BlockSchema). Source read via file.toString(). Opening line = source from the directive's start offset to end of that line, \r dropped. Children kept with the data.directiveLabel paragraph dropped, recursed. Closing fence = trailing colon run of the directive's last source line, emitted only when that fence starts at or after the last child's end offset. A refused directive without position throws.

decisions: Brace-less :::note and :::note[label] are unknown directives (remark parses both as container directives).
A known type with attributes the schema refuses (:::callout{bogus="1"}) is drawn the same way: same whole-body fallback today, one rule (typedBlockRefusal) decides both.

Pandoc ::: fences, ::name leaf lines and :name{ text lines stop refusing the body in read-only mode and render as the paragraph text the parser reads (one line under the default soft-break policy, as on GitHub); they come from the same refusal function and the Pandoc form is a colon-fenced block.
An unclosed :::note runs to the end of its container: opening line shown, content formatted, no closing line.

Out of scope and unchanged: raw HTML blocks (INFRA-342; MarkdownBody.test.tsx:276 keeps its fallback), a known block whose content rule fails (Milkdown logs createNodeInParserFail and does not throw: reproduced with :::ask{#a1} holding a heading), the Go server's document refusals.

specDepartures.spec: Change: the read-only engine draws an unknown directive as its literal lines in place and formats the rest of the text.
specDepartures.plan: The engine draws the refused directive's fence lines (opening line and closing fence) as literal text and its content as formatted Markdown, in place.
specDepartures.evidence: A :::note's content is the author's Markdown; drawing it literally keeps every mark visible inside the block, the defect itself. A literal copy of the whole block must strip the container prefix from every continuation line (remark positions: '> ' in a quote, the item indent in a list), which the fence-lines form never touches. GitHub formats what is inside an unknown fence. A1 still holds as written: ':::note', 'A note line' and ':::' show as text and the bold outside is formatted.
